
# An unfilled circle's interior

This paragraph comes before the picture and stays the anchor whenever the block right after the picture cannot be one -- another image paragraph, or a heading -- so the words below keep their own separate life.

![A ring drawing with an empty interior][ring] <!--md-layout:v1 width=45% wrap=around x=25%-->

A ring drawing reserves an outer band and leaves its own inside empty, so this long paragraph of ordinary prose, wrapping beside its silhouette line by line, eventually reaches a band low enough for a line to enter the drawing through its own unfilled centre rather than stopping at its outer edge the way an opaque picture would, which is exactly the fact this fixture exists to show the runner.

A second sentence of plain reading prose, long enough on its own that a narrow column wraps it into more than a single line, keeps this paragraph a fair test of the line planner rather than a trivial one-line case that proves very little indeed.
